style_description: An original luminous arcade playfield: almost-black negative space, restrained scientific linework, emissive targets with crisp material silhouettes, white-hot contact points and directional source-colored fragments. Not a generic cyberpunk city and not a uniform glow wash.
reference_board: Founder-provided target and disintegration screenshots; internal principles only; not included in runtime or package.

camera.view: Fixed frontal playfield with lower-center weapon emitter; reticle follows logical pointer coordinates.
camera.framing: 16:9 desktop logical canvas; retain safe margins and center playfield for aspect-ratio adaptation.
camera.perspective: Subtle target faceting and floor convergence provide 2.5D depth without harming beam collision clarity.

value_hierarchy: White-hot beam contact and active hit response are brief, highest-luminance cues.
Target silhouettes, health cracks, volatile fuse and cursor reticle remain crisp and readable.
Spectrum-coded cyan, magenta and amber beams carry distinct glyph and geometry cues.
Background linework and sparse parallax stay low-contrast and below 12% luminance.
shape_language: Neon Blocks: orthogonal beveled cubes with pixel-grid fracture. Prismatic Crystals: asymmetric faceted shards with a visible core and radial crack seams. Power-Up Cores: smooth vertical capsules containing one high-contrast ability glyph. Volatile Cores: compact jagged forms with a broken circular fuse ring. Weapon: anchored lower-center emitter and a diamond reticle.
lighting_language: Dark field, restrained local additive glows, small white contact accents, controlled persistence and no full-screen bloom. Contact flashes are brief, avoid rapid repeated screen-wide flashes, and have reduced-flash alternatives.
material_language: Blocks are luminous translucent glass over a dark interior; crystals use layered refractive facets; power cores are polished enamel with a clear symbol; volatile cores show hot internal seams and fuse pulse. Fragments inherit source material color plus impact-direction energy, with varied size, speed, spin and lifetime.
identity_invariants: Every target family reads from silhouette before hue: cube, faceted crystal, capsule, and jagged fuse core.
Spectrum matching uses both color and a displayed icon/pattern; color alone never communicates a required action.
Laser is a thin colored outer stroke with a short white core and a visible endpoint at the target surface.
Impact is staged as contact spark, directional fracture, varied ejection, differentiated afterglow and score/reward.
Overload boundary and warning text remain visible during dense effect events.
forbidden_traits: Generic cyberpunk skyline, random ornament, or dashboard clutter
Uniform glow haze or bloom that erases silhouette and contact point
Flat colored rectangles standing in for all target families
Identical particles with uniform sizes, velocities and lifetimes
Sustained strobe or a required color distinction without shape/icon backup
Reference screenshots, source image fragments or untracked third-party media shipped in the game

asset_rules.transparent_sprites: Initial prototype uses original vector geometry drawn in source code; future sprites require an asset specification, candidate retention, processing lineage, SHA-256 and review status.
asset_rules.environment: Procedural dark instrument field with low-contrast grid, sparse crosshair linework and no skyline.
asset_rules.ui: DOM text and compact instrument labels remain crisp and outside glow passes; score and overload state have persistent text and shape cues.
asset_rules.vfx: Effect curves are event-driven, staged, source-colored and bounded; reduced-effects mode lowers counts and shake while preserving hit state.
asset_rules.animation: Target hover/drift, volatile fuse, contact pulse, fracture and particle ejection use deterministic gameplay timing or independent cosmetic randomness; assess at real playback speed.

review_criteria: At 1280x720 and narrow viewport, target silhouette and health/fracture state remain readable.
Impact direction follows the beam contact normal and fragments vary materially without masking warnings or reticle.
The reference's block/crystal/capsule/volatile roles are transformed into an original cohesive system, not copied artwork.
Reduced-flash/effects and high-contrast settings preserve game information and input feedback.
style_mix_policy: Prototype geometry and procedural effects are authored in local code with no generated or external runtime asset dependency. Any later art model choice must be checked for exact checkpoint/weight license, local VRAM/runtime feasibility and measured integrated result before use.
